ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a single-phase bridge rectifier circuit; the transformer secondary u2 is connected to the diamond-shaped full bridge composed of VD1, VD2, VD3, and VD4, and the load on the right side is RL. Reasoning: During normal operation, each diode in the bridge rectifier conducts only during one half-cycle, and the problem has already given that the average DC current of a single rectifier diode over one cycle is 1 A. If one of the diodes is open-circuited, then the rectifying path in the half-cycle that requires that diode to participate is interrupted; in the other half-cycle, the conducting path composed of the opposite pair of diodes can still work. For these diodes that still conduct, the current waveform during their conducting half-cycle is the same as in normal operation, and in normal operation a single diode is also calculated as conducting for a half-cycle to obtain the cycle average current, so its average current is still 1 A.

raw_record.question_text: In the figure shown, when the single-phase bridge rectifier circuit operates normally, the average DC current through a single rectifier diode is 1 A. If one rectifier diode becomes open-circuited due to a fault, what is the average current through the remaining conducting rectifier diodes?

method.method_draft: First describe the pictured bridge: VD1-VD4 form a full bridge around the load RL. In normal operation each diode carries current for one half-cycle, and the problem states the average over a cycle for any one diode is 1 A. If one diode opens, the half-cycle requiring that diode is lost; the opposite diagonal pair remains the only conducting pair. For those remaining conducting diodes, their conduction waveform during their half-cycle is unchanged from normal operation, so their cycle-average diode current remains the same as the original single-diode average: 1 A.

method.method_draft: Interpret the faulted circuit in the image as a half-wave rectifier: one diagonal branch is broken by the open diode, while the opposite diagonal branch still connects the transformer secondary to RL during one polarity. The given 1 A normal diode average already represents the average of one half-wave conduction contribution through a bridge diode. In the half-wave fault condition, each remaining conducting diode is in series in that one surviving path, so it carries that same average current. Therefore the average current through each conducting remaining diode is 1 A.
